objective: Measure and repair the minutes-scale wallet-authority approval path without shrinking the full state-deepening soak, then land an evidence-derived per-approval latency tripwire.
falsifiable_claim: For a fixed backend and build profile, the profiling harness attributes each approval's wall and CPU time to submission, consensus/finalization, execution, state commitment, durable persistence, and proof/resolution while recording height, state/version depth, and bytes; a planted delay beyond the evidence-derived budget makes the performance qualification lane red.

code_anchors.must_contain: RESTART: all ten named lifecycles and auxiliary terms/eligibility evidence reproject exactly

adversarial_or_fault_proof: Open. The M04.8 deterministic matrix is green at 111/111 in approximately 8.4 seconds, while the complete real wallet-authority journey has demonstrated multiple-hour behavior. The first release-profile baseline completed 14/15 checks in approximately two hours: all semantic gates and all nine room-child family restart counts plus pairing/terms/eligibility counts passed, while the first post-health OutcomeRoom replay request returned 503. Earlier debug evidence returned replay 200 with the exact operation count. The verifier now treats generic health and owner-projection readiness separately through a bounded 503 retry that still fails durable unavailability; that adjustment has not been justified by another multi-hour rerun. Release mode removes debug-build ambiguity but has not removed the performance defect. Closure requires component timings across increasing height/depth, warm and restarted runs, single and batched approvals, a parity-qualified backend comparison, and a mutation that defeats the selected latency budget.
remaining_nonclaims: No numeric approval latency budget is established yet.
The current evidence does not attribute the defect solely to IAVL, Redb/WAL persistence, AFT consensus, cryptography, replay, or their composition.
Jellyfish is an in-tree qualification candidate, not a production-equivalent successor.
The scheduled soak proves only the exact profile and environment it runs.
The release-profile baseline is 14/15, not a green full-soak claim; the bounded owner-readiness retry remains to be exercised by the next scheduled run.
source_provenance: Opened 2026-08-27 from M04.8 verifier evidence: two debug-profile attempts exceeded six hours; later approval commits slowed with chain history; the release-profile baseline remained CPU-heavy and minutes-scale and ended 14/15 on the first post-health replay request while every child-family count reprojected exactly. ADR 0038 preserves the full semantic soak while separating it from the deterministic merge lane.
